name: python-dropped-import-still-called-asks
desc: removing `from ulid import ULID` while the new text still calls ULID() is the obs-py-002 pattern → ask. The additive check stays silent here because addInFileDefs folds the OLD on-disk file's import into the known set — proving this ask comes from dropped-import, not the additive check

name: python-dropped-import-removed-and-unused-clean
desc: the import AND every use are gone — a legitimate cleanup, stays silent

name: js-dropped-import-still-used-asks
desc: a removed named JS import still called below → ask
old:
import { fetchUser } from './api';
const u = fetchUser(id);

name: python-dropped-import-relocated-clean
desc: the import line is removed but the SAME name is re-imported on another line in the new text — the refactor-relocation pattern that bench/FINDINGS.md found is the dominant shape among real 'removed import still used' candidates. Every one of those spot-checks (logging, build_report, BASE_RATING) was this, not a bug. If the surviving-import check were dropped, the guard would ask on ordinary import tidying, which is the fastest way to get a default-off check left off

name: python-dropped-import-now-locally-defined-clean
desc: the import is gone and the name is now provided by a definition in the same edit — the deliberate 'stop depending on the library, implement it here' refactor. Pins the preBound suppression, the other half of FINDINGS' false-positive story: without it this legitimate edit asks, and the two clean cases here are what let the check be recommended for anyone's default-on list. Replaces go-dropped-import-excluded-clean, which caught nothing — removing the Go exclusion entirely left it silent anyway, since its qualified use never reads as an unqualified one
